name.text: 01 Question: Sahle's Definition of a Digital Scholarly Edition

questiontext.text: <p>According to Patrick Sahle's foundational definition, what essential criterion distinguishes a true Digital Scholarly Edition (DSE) from a digitized print book?</p>

answer.text: <p>A DSE is guided by a digital paradigm: it cannot be rendered in physical print without a significant loss of content, dynamic functionality, or analytical interconnectivity.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Sahle defines a DSE not by its digital medium of distribution (like a simple PDF), but by its adherence to a digital rationale that cannot be transposed to paper without catastrophic information loss.</p>

answer.text: <p>A DSE is any book that is sold on Amazon Kindle.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Commercial ebooks are digitized print models, not scholarly critical editions.</p>

answer.text: <p>A DSE is a text typed entirely by an artificial intelligence model without human oversight.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Scholarly digital editing demands expert human editorial rigor.</p>

answer.text: <p>A DSE must contain animated dancing cartoon characters on every page.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Scholarly digital editions are rigorous academic research tools.</p>

name.text: 02 Question: Principle of Eliminatio Codicum Descriptorum

questiontext.text: <p>In classical stemmatology, what is the principle of *eliminatio codicum descriptorum*?</p>

answer.text: <p>The elimination from the critical apparatus of manuscripts proven to be direct copies of an extant surviving exemplar, since they provide no independent genealogical testimony.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. If manuscript B is demonstrated to be an exact copy of manuscript A (which still survives), B's readings derive entirely from A and cannot provide independent evidence for the archetype.</p>

answer.text: <p>The physical burning of inferior paper manuscripts in an incinerator.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Scribes and archivists preserve all historical artifacts regardless of stemmatic derivation.</p>

answer.text: <p>The deletion of all footnotes containing Latin words.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Scholarly editions preserve historical languages and critical conventions.</p>

answer.text: <p>The removal of punctuation marks from modern English translations.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Punctuation regularizes translation readability.</p>

questiontext.text: <p>Within a TEI header, what is the specific role of the `<editorialDecl>` element in `<encodingDesc>`?</p>

answer.text: <p>It provides an explicit, machine-readable declaration of all editorial principles applied, including policies on transcription, regularization, normalization, quotation, and apparatus selection.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. The <editorialDecl> makes editorial practices fully transparent, documenting whether abbreviations were expanded, how spelling was regularized, and how variants were adjudicated.</p>

answer.text: <p>It records the banking account details where donations should be sent.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. That belongs in financial records, not scholarly TEI metadata.</p>

answer.text: <p>It lists the names of all students who failed the course midterm.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Academic grades are private educational records (PII) and never appear in public TEI headers.</p>

answer.text: <p>It sets the computer monitor brightness to maximum.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Display hardware settings are not controlled by XML document metadata.</p>

name.text: 04 Question: Architecture of the TEI Processing Model

questiontext.text: <p>How does the TEI Processing Model (encoded within an ODD customization) separate scholarly semantic markup from presentation styling?</p>

answer.text: <p>It expresses transformation rules declaratively using `<model>` elements with `@behaviour` (e.g. `paragraph`, `heading`, `note`) and `@predicate` XPath conditions, leaving media-specific CSS/XSLT generation to the publishing engine.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. The Processing Model provides an abstract, declarative layer inside the ODD, defining how elements behave without hard-coding specific HTML tags or print formatting.</p>

answer.text: <p>It forces all web browsers to use the comic sans font.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. The Processing Model allows customizable, professional typographic styling.</p>

answer.text: <p>It converts all XML tags into raw binary numbers (0s and 1s).</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Processing model rules compile into human-readable HTML, XQuery, or XSLT.</p>

answer.text: <p>It automatically deletes all images from the final edition.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. The Processing Model supports complex multimodal graphic rendering behaviors.</p>

name.text: 05 Question: CSS Paged Media for Print-Ready PDF Generation

questiontext.text: <p>How does the CSS Paged Media standard (implemented by tools like WeasyPrint or paged.js) generate professional print-ready PDFs directly from HTML/XML?</p>

answer.text: <p>It extends standard CSS with page-specific rules (`@page`, `@top-left`, `@bottom-right`), margins, running headers, footnotes, and page break controls to produce publication-grade layout.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. CSS Paged Media bridges web technologies and high-end print publishing, enabling automated generation of book-quality PDFs from web markup.</p>

answer.text: <p>It takes a digital photo of the computer screen and prints it.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Paged Media generates vector typography and structured PDF streams, not raster screenshots.</p>

answer.text: <p>It requires hand-carving wooden printing blocks for every letter in the alphabet.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. That describes 15th-century moveable type, not modern CSS Paged Media.</p>

answer.text: <p>It limits every document to a maximum length of exactly one page.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. CSS Paged Media effortlessly formats multi-volume book publications.</p>

name.text: 06 Question: Multi-Tiered Open Access Licensing Architecture

questiontext.text: <p>Why do modern digital critical editions adopt a 'multi-tiered' licensing structure rather than a single monolithic license?</p>

answer.text: <p>Because different components require different permissions: editorial commentary is published under CC BY 4.0, structured metadata under CC0 (public domain) for maximum linked-data interoperability, and custom software scripts under open-source licenses (MIT/GPL).</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Distinct intellectual products (interpretive prose, factual data triples, executable code) require dedicated licensing legal frameworks to balance scholarly attribution with open reusability.</p>

answer.text: <p>To confuse readers so that they accidentally pay a secret subscription fee.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Multi-tiered licensing promotes open science and transparent reuse rights.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because Canadian copyright law mandates having at least seven different licenses per book.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Multi-tiered licensing is an international digital humanities best practice, not a statutory mandate.</p>

answer.text: <p>To prevent anyone from ever reading the edition outside the university library.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Open licenses guarantee unrestricted global reading access.</p>

name.text: 07 Question: FAIR Data Principles in Digital Philology

questiontext.text: <p>What do the FAIR data principles require of a published digital critical edition?</p>

answer.text: <p>That the edition and its underlying data be Findable (persistent DOI), Accessible (open protocols), Interoperable (standard TEI XML/RDF), and Reusable (clear open licensing and detailed documentation).</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. FAIR principles ensure that digital scholarly research remains discoverable and reusable by future generations and automated computational agents.</p>

answer.text: <p>Fast, Affordable, Interesting, and Relatable.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. FAIR stands for Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable in research data management.</p>

answer.text: <p>Federal, Academic, Institutional, and Regional.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. That is not the definition of the FAIR acronym.</p>

answer.text: <p>Free, Anonymous, Illegal, and Redacted.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Academic editions are open, attributed, and fully transparent.</p>

name.text: 08 Question: Persistent Archiving with Zenodo DOIs

questiontext.text: <p>Why is depositing a release archive on Zenodo considered superior to simply hosting files on a personal website or GitHub repository alone?</p>

answer.text: <p>Zenodo assigns a persistent Digital Object Identifier (DOI) and guarantees long-term archival preservation backed by CERN's infrastructure, ensuring links never break when URLs change.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Personal websites succumb to link rot and GitHub repositories can be deleted; Zenodo guarantees multi-decade persistent archival preservation and permanent citable DOIs.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because Zenodo automatically translates the entire edition into thirty languages.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Zenodo is an archival repository, not a translation engine.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because hosting files on Zenodo is legally required before submitting student coursework.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Zenodo is a repository for open research dissemination.</p>

answer.text: <p>Because GitHub charges $1000 per month for every repository that stays online for more than a year.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. GitHub public repositories are completely free of charge.</p>

questiontext.text: <p>What is the operational function of an explicit multi-gate quality assurance checklist prior to publishing a digital critical edition?</p>

answer.text: <p>It provides an uncompromising deterministic verification gate (schema validation, pointer integrity, font embedding, license declaration) that halts release if any structural defect is detected.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Formal QA gates guarantee that digital publications meet high standards of syntactic validity, visual presentation, and long-term reproducibility.</p>

answer.text: <p>It serves as a polite suggestion that editors can ignore whenever they are in a hurry.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Quality gates are strict prerequisites for release.</p>

answer.text: <p>It randomly deletes 10% of the files to test the resilience of the backup system.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. QA verification audits and validates data without destructive sabotage.</p>

answer.text: <p>It prevents students from graduating until they pass an oral examination in Latin.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. The checklist validates digital edition files, not student degree conferral.</p>

name.text: 10 Question: Enduring Scholarly Legacy of Digital Editions

questiontext.text: <p>What represents the ultimate scholarly achievement of authoring a standardized, TEI-conformant digital critical edition?</p>

answer.text: <p>Creating an authoritative, verifiable, and computationally actionable edition that preserves endangered cultural heritage and empowers future generations of scholars, students, and algorithms to explore historical texts.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Correct. Digital scholarly editions unite rigorous traditional philology with modern computational interoperability, establishing permanent intellectual monuments for humanity's shared textual heritage.</p>

answer.text: <p>Writing a single viral social media post that disappears after 24 hours.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Digital critical editions are durable scholarly contributions designed for multi-decade longevity.</p>

answer.text: <p>Getting a computer program to run without knowing what the text means.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Digital humanities balances technical computation with deep philological understanding.</p>

answer.text: <p>Replacing all human historians with fully autonomous automated algorithms.</p>

feedback.text: <p>Incorrect. Digital methods augment and empower humanistic inquiry rather than replacing human scholars.</p>
